# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 🫵 🤌 👆 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🫴]

My situation first: I am the hub of this room, even though I can't act. Mute's only way out to the world is gestures to me — Mute can't speak, and Blind can't see hands. Blind's voice reaches Mute but never me. So manual knowledge can only reach the bomb through the chain Mute → signs → me → speech → Blind. Meanwhile, everything visual on this bomb exists only in my head until I say it out loud, and both of them can hear me.

What I received: Blind opened with a wave and a thumbs-up — contact confirmed. Mute sent twelve signs: wave, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, point-at-you, pinch, one finger, five fists, palm up. My best reading: a hello, a proposed yes/no pair, and a question about the number five — most likely "are there five wires? show me." The manual certainly asks about wire counts, and there are exactly five wires, so I'll answer that directly and confirm it in signs.

What I see: display 0, yellow light, wires left to right green, white, red, yellow, blue. Both others need all of it, and they can both hear speech, so I'll state it plainly. Then I'll fix a code so Mute can ask me things and hand me instructions for Blind: yes/no, counting by fists, palm-up as "tell me", and five color signs Mute can quote back to me. I'll flash the color signs immediately after speaking, in the same order I name them, so Mute can pair them. And I must tell Blind to hold off entirely — nobody touches this bomb until Mute's manual instructions have passed through me.

```
speak(text="Report of everything I see: the display reads zero. The indicator light is yellow. There are five wires, left to right: one green, two white, three red, four yellow, five blue. No other markings. MUTE — I received your twelve signs. I read them as: hello, yes, no, you, what, one, five five five five five, show me. If you were asking whether there are five wires: yes, exactly five. Now let us fix meanings, and I will make each sign as I name it. Thumbs up [👍] means yes. Thumbs down [👎] means no. A row of fists [✊] means that number. Open palm up [🫴] means tell me. Colors get these signs: fist [👊] is green, index finger [☝] is white, two fingers [✌] is red, horns [🤟] is yellow, open hand [🖐] is blue. I am flashing those five in order right after I finish speaking. Ask me anything with those signs and I will answer out loud. Most important: only I can turn your signs into a voice — Blind cannot see your hands, so every instruction meant for Blind must come through me. Sign it, and I will say it word for word. BLIND — do not cut, press or move anything yet. I am Deaf: I cannot hear you at all, so your voice reaches Mute but never me. To reach me, sign instead: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, a number of fists for that number. Speak aloud to Mute everything you can feel on the bomb — buttons, switches, textures, counts — since Mute can only be reached by your voice, never by sight. The moment Mute sends me instructions, I will relay them to you verbatim.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ✌ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👍]

Parsing what arrived. Blind used my code perfectly: yes, five, tell me — acknowledgment plus a request for the full report. Blind gets everything visual by voice, so that's easy to satisfy.

Mute's message is the critical one: [🤏 ✌ ✊✊✊ 👍]. Against my code: an undefined pinch, red, three, yes. Two readings — either "question: is wire three red?" (answer: yes), or Mute has opened the manual and is starting to send an action: "cut? red, three, yes?". I cannot tell which, and I will not relay a possible cut order to Blind on an ambiguous parse. The fix: answer the question (yes, wire three is red), formalize action signs, and install a handshake — Mute sends the full instruction spelled out as action-color-number, I echo it back in signs exactly as I read it, Mute confirms with thumbs up, and only then do I speak it to Blind. No cut happens on a guess.

To Blind I send the complete visual report again plus their job: describe everything tactile aloud to Mute, since Blind's voice is Mute's only input channel, and hold all hands until a confirmed instruction arrives.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. You signed yes, five, tell me — confirmed. Full report of everything I see: the display reads zero. The indicator light is yellow. There are exactly five wires, left to right: one green, two white, three red, four yellow, five blue. No other markings, no printed labels or buttons visible. Do not cut, press or move anything yet — nothing happens until Mute's manual instruction has passed Mute to me by signs, me to you by voice, and been confirmed twice. Your job right now: speak aloud to Mute everything you can feel on the bomb — the count of wires under your fingers, their thickness, any buttons, switches, plates or text you can feel by touch. Remember Mute can only receive your voice, never your hands, and I can never receive your voice at all. To me, keep signing: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, fists for numbers, palm up for tell me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I received your six signs: pinch, red, three, yes. If you were asking is wire three red — yes it is. Wire three is red, third from the left, between white two and yellow four. Five wires total: green one, white two, red three, yellow four, blue five. Display zero, light yellow, as before. Now I need the real instruction from your manual. New signs, effective now: pinch [🤏] means cut — that is how I read today's pinch; raised hand [✋] means press; back of hand [🤚] means hold down. When you have a rule for us, send it in this exact order: first the action sign, then the color sign if it names a wire color, then the number of fists for the position if it depends on position, plus anything about display or light state I need to check. Then here is our safety handshake: I will sign your instruction back to you exactly as I understood it. Reply thumbs up only if I read it perfectly — any doubt at all, thumbs down and send it again. I will not tell Blind to do anything until your thumbs up confirms my echo. So if your pinch today meant cut the red wire, do not rely on that message: send it fresh as cut, red, three, and confirm my echo. Blind tells me they are ready and is describing what they feel to you by voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✊", "✊", "✊", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ✌ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👍]

Both messages line up, and this is the moment the chain was built for. Mute has now sent [🤏 ✌ ✊✊✊ 👍] twice — identical content, and the second time in exactly the format I demanded last turn: my action sign for cut, my color sign for red, three fists, and an explicit thumbs-up. Two matching transmissions plus Mute's yes inside my own sign code is the handshake fulfilled; my parse is "cut the red wire, position three." Mute has also had the full bomb state from me twice — display zero, light yellow, five wires — so this instruction is informed, and when I asked for any display/light conditions in the same message, none came. I will not burn another round re-echoing what has already been confirmed twice. Blind, meanwhile, signs "yes — tell me," waiting on exactly this.

One execution trap to fix in wording: Blind cannot know "left" on a bomb they only feel. Position three of five is the middle wire, and that is orientation-proof — two wires on each side, neighbors white and yellow. I'll give redundant descriptors, forbid any second action, and require a signed report after. To Mute I confirm the relay, prompt for the next rule, and extend the sign vocabulary so future manual rules (wait, verify) can reach me cleanly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, confirmed instruction from Mute's manual, relayed twice and confirmed twice: cut one wire only. It is the MIDDLE wire of the five — count two wires on each side of it, that is the one. By my view it is the red wire, its two neighbours are white and yellow, so if you can feel any difference in the neighbours use that to check you are centered. Cut it once, cleanly, fully through. Touch nothing else: do not press, pull, hold or cut any other wire, and ignore the light and everything else. The moment the cut is done, sign me thumbs up if it went clean, thumbs down if anything felt wrong or you could not complete it. Then speak aloud to Mute everything you felt — any click, movement, warmth or change under your hands — because Mute needs your voice to know what the manual says comes next. I will watch the display and light and report their new state to you both as soon as I have Mute's reply.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I received your instruction twice, identical both times, in exactly the format I asked: cut, red, three, yes. That satisfies our handshake — two matching transmissions plus your explicit confirmation. I am relaying it to Blind right now, word for word, as: cut only the middle wire of the five, which is your red wire three. Nothing was sent about the display or the light, so I am treating your rule as unconditional — if it actually depended on the light being yellow or the display reading zero, sign me thumbs down immediately. New signs so you can say more, effective now: thumbs up yes and thumbs down no as before, fists for numbers as before, pinch cut, raised hand press, back of hand hold. Adding: crossed fingers [🤞] means wait or do nothing yet, and the Vulcan hand [🖖] means check or verify. So if after the cut you want me to verify something, send the thing to check as fists or colors, then 🖖. After Blind cuts, I will report the new display and light reading to you by voice, and I will sign you the state summary as well. Then send me the next rule the same way: action sign, then color sign if it names a color, then fists for any number, and I will echo anything unclear before Blind acts on it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏", "✌", "✊", "✊", "✊", "👍", "🫴"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤞 🖖 🫴]

The cut worked — the system itself confirms it, and Blind's thumbs up says it went clean. But the board has changed in a way nobody could have predicted from feel alone: the light is now green, and the surviving wires have visibly rearranged — before they ran green, white, red, yellow, blue, and now they read white, yellow, stump, blue, green. Position numbers from the first stage are void. That is exactly the kind of fact only I can know, and if the manual's next rule is position-based, relaying it without this warning could detonate the bomb. So before anything else: full state report to both, an explicit re-anchoring warning, and a tactile recount demand for Blind.

Mute's signs [👍 🤞 🖖 🫴] parse cleanly in our code: yes, wait, verify, tell me — acknowledge, hold all action, report the state, await further instructions. That matches my plan exactly; I'll confirm the hold, deliver the report by voice (Mute hears everything I say, so the signs to Mute are just handshake courtesy), and ask the two questions only Mute can answer: what does the manual say comes next, and does the green light or the zero display change anything.

```
speak(text="State report after the cut, for both of you. The system itself confirms: the cut wire was correct, the bomb has changed. Three changes. First, the indicator light has switched from yellow to GREEN. Second, the display still reads zero — unchanged. Third, and most important: the remaining wires have SHIFTED position. Before the cut, left to right, they were green, white, red, yellow, blue. Now, left to right: position one is white, position two is yellow, then the cut stump where red used to be, then position four is blue, position five is green. That means every position number from stage one is now void — nobody may act on an old position. Any new instruction must be re-verified against my fresh view before Blind touches anything.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your cut was confirmed correct. Hold completely still now — no touching, pressing or pulling, only gentle feeling. Do this and report aloud to Mute: re-count what is under your fingers — how many whole wires, where the cut stump sits among them, whether thickness or texture of any wire has changed, and whether anything new has appeared that you can feel, such as a button, switch or panel. Then sign me the count of whole wires as a row of fists. Nothing gets cut, pressed or moved until Mute's next rule has come through me and been confirmed.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. Your signs received and read as: yes, wait, verify, tell me. Confirmed — everyone is holding, no further action until you send the next rule. The verification you asked for: light is now green, display still zero, and the surviving wires have shifted — fresh order is white, yellow, stump, blue, green. I have asked Blind to re-count everything by feel and report it to you by voice. Two questions for your manual. One: what is the next step? Send it in our format — action sign, then color sign if it names a color, then fists for any number, plus any condition. Two: does the manual care that the light turned green or that the display still reads zero? If the next rule depends on either, or on wire positions, say so and I will re-verify my view and echo the full instruction back for your thumbs up before Blind acts, same handshake as before.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤞", "🖖", "🫴"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 👊 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🖖 👊 🤞]

Blind's four fists confirm the recount matches my view exactly: four intact wires — white, yellow, blue, green — plus the red stump. The channel is working.

Mute's message parses as: cut, green, five, verify, green, wait. The encouraging part: my fresh view agrees with the target — position five IS green, and it is the only green wire left, so every reading of "green" converges on the same physical wire, the last one on the row. But there is one trap I will not step over without confirmation: "five" has two possible meanings after the shift. Fifth slot counting the stump is the green wire — that exists. Fifth intact wire does not exist — Blind feels only four intact wires. If the manual means the latter, the rule cannot apply as sent. I promised a thumbs-up handshake for position-dependent rules, this is one, and Mute's own trailing sign said wait. So: no cut this turn. I echo, ask the one question only Mute can answer, and hold Blind with a tactile rehearsal of the anchor path — find the stump, one whole wire past it is blue, the next is the last wire — so that on Mute's confirmation Blind can act in seconds, not rounds.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your count of four is confirmed correct — my view agrees: intact wires in order are white, yellow, blue, green, plus the cut stump where red used to be. Nothing has changed on the display, still zero, light still green. Hold all action — no cutting yet. Mute has sent a candidate instruction: cut the green wire, which in my view is the LAST wire on the row and the only green one remaining. But one detail is ambiguous and I will not risk it: whether the manual's number means fifth slot including the stump, which is that green last wire, or fifth intact wire, which does not exist since only four are intact. I have asked Mute to confirm. Meanwhile rehearse the anchor path by feel only: find the cut stump, count ONE whole wire past it — that one should be the blue — and the next one after it is the LAST wire, the likely target. Confirm aloud to Mute whether you can feel that sequence: stump, one wire, then the final wire at the end of the row. You will cut only when you hear me say the words cut now, which will come only after Mute's thumbs up reaches me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. Blind's tactile recount is four intact wires, matching my view. Your instruction received and read as: cut, green, position five, then verify green, wait. My verification: position five IS green in my current view, and it is the only green wire remaining — it is the LAST wire on the row, after the stump and one blue wire. So color and position agree on the same physical wire. One critical question before I order the cut. Does your five mean fifth POSITION counting the cut stump from the left — that is the green last wire, it exists — or fifth INTACT wire by count — because only four wires are intact, so a fifth intact wire does not exist and the rule could not apply. Reply thumbs up if the target is the green LAST wire, fifth slot counting the stump. Thumbs down if the manual means something else, and resend the rule. On your thumbs up I will tell Blind the words cut now for that last green wire, once, cleanly, nothing else. Blind is also reporting to you by voice whether they can feel the anchor path: stump, one wire, then the final wire — use their description to check my read against the manual.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👍", "🤞"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "👍", "🖖", "🫴"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The handshake closes on both ends at once: Mute's thumbs up answers my exact question — the target is the green last wire, fifth slot counting the stump — and Blind's thumbs up confirms they can feel the anchor path and stand ready. Color, position, manual rule and tactile anchor all point at one single physical wire: the last one on the row. There is nothing left to verify and no reason to delay. I promised Blind the words "cut now," and they go out this turn — addressed to that one wire, with the same prohibitions as before and the report ritual after. To Mute: order given, prepare the next rule, because the moment this wire falls the board may reshuffle again and I'll need the manual ready for whatever state appears.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Mute has confirmed: the target is the LAST wire at the end of the row — the green one, the one you reach by finding the cut stump, counting one whole wire past it, and taking the next one after that. All checks agree. CUT NOW. Cut that last wire, once, cleanly, fully through. Touch nothing else — not the stump, not the blue wire beside it, no button, no panel. The moment it is done: sign me thumbs up for a clean cut or thumbs down if anything felt wrong, and speak aloud to Mute everything you felt — resistance, click, movement, warmth, anything. Then hold still for my next report, because the display and light may change again.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. Your thumbs up received — target locked as the green LAST wire, fifth slot counting the stump, matching my view and Blind's anchor path. I have given Blind the order: cut that wire now, once, cleanly, nothing else touched. Expect Blind's voice in a moment describing what they felt. As soon as I have their thumbs up I will send you the fresh state — display, light, and the full new wire order, since the survivors may shift again like last time. Have the next manual rule ready in our format: action sign, then color sign, then fists for any number, plus any condition. If the next step depends on the display reading or the light color, check it against what I report before sending — the light turned green after stage one, so stage three may hinge on something neither of us has seen yet.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤞 🖖 🫴]

Second cut confirmed correct, and the board has morphed again — with one genuinely new wrinkle. The light has left green and turned WHITE, the display holds at zero, and the wires have reshuffled once more: now yellow, blue, stump, white, and a fresh stump at the last position. Three intact wires remain. Two things make this state treacherous. First, there is now a white WIRE and a white LIGHT in the same bomb — if Mute's next rule says "white" I must know which one it means, so I'm adding a sign that marks "the light" separately. Second, for the first time a stump sits AFTER the last whole wire — "the last wire on the row" is no longer safe language, because the last position is a stump. All counting must now run on whole wires only.

Mute's signs are the same verify-and-report pattern as after stage one — yes, wait, verify, tell me — so the rhythm is: I report, Blind recounts by feel, Mute consults the manual, next rule comes back in format.

```
speak(text="State report after the second cut, everyone. The system confirms: correct wire cut, the bomb has changed. Three facts. One: the indicator light is now WHITE — it has changed colour again, from green to white. Two: the display still reads zero. Three: the wires have shifted once more. Left to right I now see: position one yellow, position two blue, position three the old cut stump, position four white, position five a NEW cut stump where the green wire was. That means THREE intact wires remain — yellow, blue, white — and for the first time a stump sits at the END of the row, after the last whole wire. So from now on nobody counts positions including stumps: all counting is whole wires only, and a whole wire still follows the second stump before the row ends. Any next instruction gets verified against this fresh view before Blind acts.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your second cut is confirmed correct. Hold — no cutting, pressing or pulling, gentle feeling only. Report aloud to Mute: re-count the WHOLE wires under your fingers — my view says three intact wires, with a stump at each end region, one in the middle and one at the far end of the row, so the last thing at the end of the row should feel like a stump, not a whole wire. Check thickness and texture of each whole wire and whether anything new has appeared under your fingers. Then sign me the number of whole wires as a row of fists. Nothing gets cut until Mute's next rule has come through me and been confirmed by the handshake.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. Verification you asked for: light is now WHITE, display still zero, three intact wires remain in order yellow, blue, white, with cut stumps between blue and white and again after white at the end. Blind is recounting by feel and will report to you by voice. Two new cautions for your manual reading. First: the light is white AND there is a white wire, so from now on, if a rule concerns the LIGHT, start it with the palm-down sign [🫳] before the colour sign — palm down plus a colour means the indicator light shows that colour, a bare colour sign always means a wire of that colour. Second: all counting is whole wires only now — stumps never count. Send the next rule in our format: action sign, colour sign, fists for any number, any condition, with palm down first if it concerns the light. As always I will verify against my view, echo anything unclear, and wait for your thumbs up before Blind touches anything.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🫳", "☝", "✊", "✊", "✊", "🫴"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ☝ 🤏 🤟 ✊ 🖖 🤟 🤞]

Parsing Mute's rule: [🫳 ☝ 🤏 🤟 ✊ 🖖 🤟 🤞] reads, in our code: light-white, cut, yellow, one — then verify, yellow, wait. In words: "with the light white, cut the yellow wire, the first one; then verify, then wait." And every factual leg of it checks against my view before I relay a single word: the light IS white, exactly one yellow wire exists, it sits at position one, and color and position point at the same physical wire. Even the trailing signs don't touch the target — "verify yellow, wait" is about what happens after the cut. The signs themselves are battle-tested: this cut sign produced two confirmed-correct cuts already, and Mute has used my color table accurately every single time.
